Keywords: Nevryui’s intervention and princely change in 1252
RagShortTexts: Alexander subsequently gained Vladimir’s grand principality.

Variants.Content: Mongol intervention displaced Andrei in 1252, followed by Alexander’s accession in Vladimir. Dynastic rivalry and overlord recognition intertwine. Residents bear campaigning and collection, while factions differ over blame; new orders still need local implementation.
Changing rule requires verified command. Former comrades may acquire different patrons, making identification and protected supply important after leadership changes.
Overlord support changes dynastic strength but not automatic local allegiance. Retainers, collection and grievances determine usable authority after accession.
Households may not know court dealings but know their losses. Unrecognized prior payments turn succession into repeated demands, increasing the value of witnesses.
